_readme: Ground-truth dataset for parser evaluation. One entry per plan. Filled from the drawing's own text + user answers. Used by batch_eval scorecards now; later = labelled dataset for the Phase-2 fine-tune flywheel.

envelope_rebaseline.scale_source: column_box_12in -> room_dim_text (printed room dimensions, read by OCR)
evidence: R-2: 6 rooms checked against the sheet's own printed dimensions - median match 61.5% -> 96.4%, worst 86.1%, 0 rooms off by >20% (was 6 of 6)
the 1.37-1.40x area ratio was CONSTANT across a 5x room-size range (26 to 138 sqft), so it is multiplicative (scale), not additive (wall inclusion)
door gap: median snapped door 3.81 ft vs schedule D1 3'3" = 1.17x, agrees with the 1.196x correction
stilt: printed STILT FLOOR 1900 sqft ~= printed flats 1705 + common 246 = 1951 (2.6%), corroborating the printed figures as the true floor plate
envelope_rebaseline.known_open: R-8 built-up knowingly RED at 68.1% (1161 parsed vs 1705 printed): room COVERAGE is short - 9 pockets found of ~16 rooms. Sizes are right; coverage is the next gap. R-8 must RISE as coverage improves, never silently fall.
envelope_rebaseline.rule: PLAN-READING-RULES 0.1: a golden may be re-baselined ONLY when the drawing's own printed data disproves it.

r2_finding_2026_08_11.verdict: REJECTED - room detection on this sheet is NOT trustworthy
r2_finding_2026_08_11.diagnosis: UNDER-SEGMENTATION, not a scale error. 13 of 14 rooms measure ~57% of their printed size while r0 measures 3.2x (530.5 vs 163.7 printed) - a constant ratio would mean scale, this scatter means rooms are merging and leaking into each other.
r2_finding_2026_08_11.units: sheet is in METRES (prints 3.43x4.04 etc); 44 metric pairs read. Feeding them to the scale voter derived 33.7 pt/ft against the column-box 8.8 - a 3.8x disagreement - which would have shipped a 2.75 ft building. The §0.1 consistency cross-check rejected OUR derivation and kept the column-box scale; sheet stays flagged NEEDS REVIEW.
r2_finding_2026_08_11.do_not: do not accept a room-count or area improvement on this sheet without R-2 rising above 80%

balcony_artefact_removed_2026_08_15.status: ARTEFACT REMOVED - UNVERIFIABLE, not an unexplained movement
balcony_artefact_removed_2026_08_15.cause: balcony was `foot_ext - foot`, a difference between two masks. It measured how far the ring bridging reached outside the raster, not a balcony. Deleted corpus-wide on 15 Aug when balcony became a direct measurement from the drawn railing edge (B-1/B-4).
balcony_artefact_removed_2026_08_15.why_the_same_as_FLOOR_PLAN: FLOOR PLAN lost the identical artefact (42.7 sqft) for the identical reason, and there the replacement is CHECKED: flat-1 measures 3.92 ft against a printed 4'0". Here there is no such check.
balcony_artefact_removed_2026_08_15.why_unverifiable: this sheet prints no area statement (R-8 blind) and classifies 0 of 38 railing runs, because it has no trusted paired walls so `ends_on_wall` is always 0. Nothing on this sheet can confirm or refute the 354.5.
balcony_artefact_removed_2026_08_15.do_not: do not treat this as evidence the new balcony rule is wrong OR right on this sheet; it is silent here. R-2 58.6 guard still stands.

two_views_finding_2026_08_15.evidence: vertical empty band at x 38-42 ft with ZERO lines crossing it (contrast neelachala FIRST FLOOR, whose horizontal band has 11 terrace-hatch lines spanning it and is therefore ONE building)
two_views_finding_2026_08_15.currently_parsed_as_one: YES - every room appears TWICE at dx ~43.5 ft (dining 164.7/164.6, bedrooms 87.5/87.4, 84.6/84.4, kitchens 50.8/49.9)
two_views_finding_2026_08_15.explains: the 80.0 x 47.8 ft extent = two ~40 ft plans side by side; and the 530.5 sqft blob that wrecks R-2 (3.24x its printed size) STRADDLES the band at x 35.1-61.1, merging rooms from both plans
two_views_finding_2026_08_15.does_NOT_explain: the 19% scale error (printed room dims imply ppf 7.14 against the column-box 8.80). That scale is derived from column boxes, independent of the extent, so it is a SEPARATE defect.
two_views_finding_2026_08_15.do_not: do not accept any area or room-count improvement here until the two views are separated; R-2 58.6 guard stands

neelachala FIRST FLOOR.pdf.parsing_strategy: CORRECTED 2026-08-15: this sheet is TWO COMPLETE COPIES OF THE SAME PLAN stacked vertically - NOT wings, NOT sections. An 8 ft empty band at y 98-108 ft separates blocks at 0-98 and 108-182 ft; 38'-3" overall is printed twice (y 97.4 and 109.4); both halves carry full room labels and dimensions; FIRST FLOOR PLAN titles the lower block at y 185.9. Both draw on the SAME layers (0, chhaja, a-text), so only POSITION can separate them. Fix = a VIEW SPLITTER, not wing-splitting. (previous wording: 'split the layout sheet into individual flat/wing modules' - wrong diagnosis)

r2_2026_08_15_INSTRUMENTED.status: PROMOTED TO INSTRUMENTED - the 31.1% verdict of 11 Aug is WITHDRAWN
r2_2026_08_15_INSTRUMENTED.cause_of_the_old_failure: NOT structural. `room_dims._PAIR_RE` could not read the hyphen form `11'-5"` - this sheet uses it everywhere, FLOOR PLAN uses it nowhere - so 4 dimension pairs were read from 359 tokens and exactly ONE room ever matched. Fixed 15 Aug by making the foot-inch separator optional. The rooms were never wrong; the reader could not read the sheet's notation.
r2_2026_08_15_INSTRUMENTED.guard_removed: the 'no improvements accepted below 80%' guard is LIFTED. R-2 96.8 is now a RATCHET, pinned by tests/test_room_dims.py::test_first_floor_r2_ratchet

r2_2026_08_15_INSTRUMENTED.R8_STILL_BLIND: this sheet prints NO area statement, so R-8 cannot be computed here. Coverage is unmeasured; only room SIZES are checked.
r2_2026_08_15_INSTRUMENTED.caveat_two_plans: its 2 reported balconies (34.2 and 33.7 sqft) both sit in the LOWER plan block (y 110 and 148 ft). This sheet carries TWO COMPLETE COPIES of the same plan - see two_plans_finding_2026_08_15 - so the view splitter WILL change that count.

superseded.verdict: FAILS R-2 - room detection on this sheet is NOT trustworthy
superseded.different_from_ghatikia: YES - probably a DIFFERENT disease. GHATIKIA fails across 14 matched rooms with a consistent ~57% shortfall (systematic under-segmentation). Here only ONE printed dimension matched a room at all (r1: measured 164.2 vs printed 97.2, 31.1%), so the headline is a single sample: the primary failure is that R-2 cannot MATCH this sheet's printed dimensions to rooms, and r1 reading 1.7x its label suggests merging. NOT INVESTIGATED - flag only.
superseded.do_not: do not accept a room-count or area improvement on this sheet without R-2 rising above 80% across several rooms

_data_policy: plans/ = raw drawings (gitignored, confidential). ground_truth.json + INDEX.txt = the LABELS, small text, tracked in git so every change is versioned and reversible - nothing gets messed up. batch_eval reads labels, never writes them; parser outputs go to out/ (gitignored). Later: human-corrected scene.json snapshots join this file as training pairs (Phase-2 flywheel).

_cad_upload_v1_1.what: upload accepts .dxf/.dwg (+ existing pdf/png/jpg): server/cad_vector.py re-draws DXF into an in-memory layered PDF (OCG = DXF layer names) and the standard pdf_vector engine parses it with ppf_hint = EXACT scale from CAD units (no guessing)
_cad_upload_v1_1.units_rule: $INSUNITS is only a candidate (often wrong; ezdxf defaults new files to metres) - every unit guess is scored: building width 12-400 ft + dominant column 0.5-2.2 ft
_cad_upload_v1_1.dwg_rule: dwg2dxf (LibreDWG) looked up on PATH or DWG_CONVERTER env; Dockerfile builds it best-effort; absent -> friendly 'Save As DXF' 422 message
_cad_upload_v1_1.columns_rule: scale_src=cad_units accepts any column 9-24in (12in-only rule kept for PDFs)
